cases.name: Helen Terry
cases.about:
“She was very kind, very loving. That’s why we can’t even imagine something like that even happening to her — totally uncalled for,” said her brother, John Mays. “We missed her dearly for 44 years and to this day we still miss her, but due to the circumstances, we know she can’t come back. But she’s always been in our hearts and always will be," Mays said.

Helen Terry lived a gentle and kind life. She served her country in the military and worked hard after leaving the service to raise her baby, her family said.
cases.narrative: On 8/28/1980, she was found deceased, stabbed 13 times, in her apartment and her 1-year-old son was discovered alone inside the the home where her body was discovered. Terry desperately fought her assailant at her apartment in Sacramento’s Valley Hi / North Laguna neighborhood, police theorized at the time. Furniture overturned and blood was spattered while her baby watched his mother suffer 13 stab wounds during the assault, according to The Sacramento Bee’s previous reporting. A suspect had scrawled a racial slur over the bathroom door and vanity mirror, authorities said. Terry was Black.

cases.name: Mary Kate Tibbitts
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "In her professional career, Kate held a variety of management, sales, and administrative positions, most recently as an Examination Analyst for the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors, and Geologists. She was always respected for her work ethic and a job well done, while always understanding the value of a work-life balance. She credited her many experiences in her career and in life with making her the well rounded person she was.
Kate was highly involved in both community and charitable endeavors including, for many years, Christmas Promise and the SPCA. She never missed working at her beloved SPCA Doggie Dash and also enjoyed other walkathons for charity. She had a passion for the arts and volunteered at Music Circus and Community Center productions for many years. To Kate, her civic duty was much more than the mere act of voting; she regularly worked on elections at voting precincts.
Kate was passionate about traveling with friends and family, including many hiking and scuba diving trips. Her travels included visiting her niece in Montreal, cruising with family to Alaska, touring in Europe, and diving in the Galapagos Islands, Philippines and Mexico.
When at home, Kate loved walking daily (often multiple times) with various friends and neighbors, and usually with her dogs. She was a life-long learner and a voracious reader. She loved collecting unique pieces of art and furniture. One could get a feeling for who Kate was just by walking through her home.
Kate was a member of the Catholic Church, most recently attending Mass at Holy Spirit Parish Church and St. Francis of Assisi. She also attended bible study at both Holy Spirit and at Harvest Church of Elk Grove. Her spirituality took many forms. In particular, in 2016, Kate spent over a month as she reflected on her life and connection to God by walking The Camino de Santiago (Way of St. James) in France and Spain.
Family was very important to Kate. She spent many weekends with her family at "the ranch" and took joy in spending time with all of her nieces and nephews. Watching or attending 49er games with family and friends was another favorite activity. Kate loved helping plan and participate in biennial Arkoosh family reunions.
Kate was loved and cherished by so many. She was a connector, interconnecting people from different walks of life, which always ended in friendship. She knew most of her neighbors and will be greatly missed on the block. She was always ready to engage in conversation and be of service."

cases.name: Kimberly Monique Sosa
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Kimberly Monique Sosa was born on January 2, 1981 in Carlsbad, New Mexico to Rose Ann Gomez and Castulo Sosa. She earned her wings on January 5, 2022 in Sacramento, California. Kim moved to Bakersfield, CA in 1981 as an infant with her mother (who was pregnant with Jeremy at the time), Aunt Lorina and cousin Melissa. In Spring of 1995, she moved to Sacramento, CA. Years later she became a mother of three children, who were all born in Sacramento. Kim was a driven woman who persevered the dualities of life. Always keeping an uplifted spirit through the good and challenging times.

She was always supportive and the best listener--making you feel as if you were the only one on earth.

Kim played many roles in our family as a mother, daughter, “ Mimaw” (grandmother), sister, niece, cousin, and above all she was a loving friend.

Her friendship carried over to her professional life at Starbucks where she worked loyally for 8 years. Her infectious spirit was so contagious that upon her passing they closed the location for her fellow colleagues to grieve.

In 2020 Kim’s drive was in full force. Graduating with her GED while simultaneously obtaining her certification in Medical billing, working and raising her youngest daughter. Waking up as early as 4am for morning shifts and arranging her schedule for Bella.

In the same year, she purchased her first new car; a red cherry Kia Sol. Symbolizing another milestone of her achievements. This was her time to shine. And we could hear it through her music when she came down the street.

In 2021, Kim revealed the news that she was going to be a grandmother for the third time. She counted down the days for Laylinas birth and spent every chance she could to be with her eldest granddaughter Penelope-who called her “Mimaw” and her daughter Delilah. She was also so proud of her son Adrian graduating high school and his plans to enlist in the Army. Her best year wasn’t over, later in the year she was hired for a career position at a local orthopedic office as a medical biller. We were all so proud of her."
cases.narrative: On 1/5/2022, her body was found her body in a parking garage on K Street in Sacramento, CA.
